name: What happens if rain hits during a pool renovation?

mainEntity.name: How does rain affect an in-progress pool renovation in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How does rain affect an in-progress pool renovation in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rain is one of the most common reasons pool renovation schedules slip, especially when the pool is open to the elements. Moisture can interfere with prep work, plaster application, tile setting, and curing, depending on the phase of construction. Contractors may need to cover work areas, delay material installation, or revisit surfaces that were exposed to water. In Los Angeles, seasonal rain is usually manageable, but even a short storm can shift the sequence of tasks. Homeowners should ask how the contractor handles weather delays and whether the schedule includes buffer time. It also helps to know whether the contractor has protection protocols for open shells, exposed plumbing, and nearby hardscape. A renovation plan that assumes perfect weather is risky; one that plans for interruptions is more realistic and usually less stressful.
acceptedAnswer.description: Rain can delay demolition, shell prep, curing, and some finish applications during a pool renovation. If the pool is open or newly prepared, crews may need to pause work, protect surfaces, and reschedule certain steps until conditions are dry enough.
